title: Mechanism-based targeting of unique survival signaling in residual tumors
text:
Targeted cancer therapies have the exciting potential to selectively kill malignant cells while sparing healthy
tissues, as evidenced by their often remarkable upfront activity in patients. However, in nearly all patients, a
subset of residual cancer cells survive therapy and later emerge to give rise to resistant disease that is very
difficult to treat. In this proposal, we build on our recent discovery of unique biological processes related to cell
death regulation and DNA repair that are activated in residual cancer cells, proposing mechanistic studies that
will significantly expand our understanding of residual tumor biology while directly nominating therapeutic
strategies to eliminate this critical tumor cell population.

title: Functional Genomic Core
text: The Functional Genomics (FG) shared resource supports Duke Cancer Institute investigators by providing a broad range of services to facilitate the application of functional genomics and high-throughput screening technologies to the study of cancer. Through investments in CRISPR, RNAi, Open Reading Frame (ORF) and compound collections, as well as high-throughput screening infrastructure, we have assembled stateof- the-art technological platforms for functional studies in both high-and low-throughput applications. The FG provides expertise and assistance in developing and implementing genetic screens in arrayed or pooled format, as well as custom services for the creation of individual knockout, knockin or overexpression cellular models. In addition, FG enables screening of varied compound collections with either cell-based or biochemical assays for chemical genetic or drug discovery studies. FG also provides access to advanced instrumentation for screen-related or standalone assays, including multimodal plate readers and a highcontent screening (HCS) system for image-based analysis. Finally, the FG is dedicated to developing and adapting new techniques and reagents to better support the needs of DCI investigators, enabling them to keep pace with the rapidly evolving field of functional genomics. In 2022, Functional Genomics provided services to 61 DCI investigators, 67% of all users, and represented 6 DCI Research Programs. Use of the shared resource by DCI members contributed to 39 publications over the current project period, demonstrating the value of services offered by this shared resource. The FG shared resource is primarily supported by cost recovery through service fees, with additional institutional support to subsidize operating costs.

title: Decoupling sex chromosome and sex hormone regulation of cardiac myofibroblast activation
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because we will improve our understanding of sex-specific
cardiac remodeling during myocardial fibrosis using bioengineered models of disease and identify paths toward
sex-specific heart failure therapeutics. This project is relevant to the mission of the NIH, because heart failure
impacts over six million people in the United States, and identifying sex-based heart failure therapeutics would
help resolve gender health disparities in heart failure treatments.

title: Dissecting the role of Notch signaling in the pancreatic cancer microenvironment.
text:
Notch signaling regulates pancreatic tumor epithelium. Its role in the tumor microenvironment is less clear. We
will dissect compartment specific Notch signaling (Aim 1); study Notch-driven myeloid polarization of T cells (Aim
2), and test the role of Notch inhibition of T cell function and activity (Aim 3) in the pancreatic tumor
microenvironment.

title: 5mC and 5hmC DNA alterations as sensitive and specific biomarkers for the non-invasive early detection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
text:
We will perform a comprehensive and genome-wide evaluation of cell-free DNA methylation biomarkers in blood
samples as potential noninvasive biomarkers for the early detection of pancreatic cancers. Moreover, we will
gauge the potential for anticipating the diagnosis in clinical samples collected before PDAC clinical diagnosis
during the PLCO Trial. Successful identification of such biomarkers will provide a major advance in the
management of this fatal disease.

title: Molecular basis for CRISPR-associated transposons and RNA-guided transcriptional regulation
text:
RNA-guided biological systems, such as CRISPR-Cas, can be easily tailored to target any
sequence in the genome, making them valuable tools in both research and medicine. Our
research seeks to understand how RNA-guided systems, especially those involved in DNA
insertion and gene regulation, function at a molecular level. Our work is poised to unlock their
full potential, contributing to further advances in biotechnology and genome editing.

title: Elucidating spatiotemporal dynamics of nascent extracellular matrix in response to platinum treatment in ovarian cancer
text:
Dysregulation of the extracellular matrix (ECM) composition critically contributes to ovarian cancer’s ability to
resist treatment. While this unidirectional relationship is well elucidated, it largely remains to be determined if
chemotherapy alters newly synthesized ECM further aggravating chemoresistance. Using tissue engineering
and metabolic labeling approaches we will track spatiotemporal changes of ECM in response to treatment to
directly apply significant insights to women suffering this particularly deadly form of cancer.

title: A Phase 1 Study to Evaluate Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cells Targeting TAG72 in Patients with Recurrent Epithelial Ovarian Cancer
text:
Patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) become resistant to platinum-based chemotherapies
after which they have few treatment options and very short lifespan. The proposal clinically evaluates a newly
developed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy against EOC by redirecting the patients’ own immune
T cells against the tumor target TAG72, which is highly expressed on the tumor cells. We have designed this
potent immunotherapy to improve outcomes for patients with advanced EOC.

title: Innate-Immune Activating Nanoparticles for Cancer Treatment
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health as these studies will generate new fundamental knowledge
in nanotechnology for biomedical applications and address the current technical limitations in immunotherapy
against solid cancer.

title: Structure-function studies of visual arrestin
text:
We propose to elucidate the molecular mechanism of arrestin-1 binding to rhodopsin, design arrestin-1
mutants that compensate for defects of rhodopsin phosphorylation in vivo, and identify novel interaction
partners of arrestin-1 in rod photoreceptors. To this end, we propose to use direct binding assay with
phosphorylated and unphosphorylated light-activated and dark rhodopsin, in vivo electroretinography in
mice, ex vivo single cell recordings of rod photoreceptors, and in vivo proximity labeling with subsequent
mass-spectrometry.

title: Single-cell mitochondrial mutation lineage tracing of non-dysplastic and dysplastic Barrett's esophagus
text:
Barrett's esophagus (BE) is the only known precursor lesion for esophageal adenocarcinoma and little is known
about the progression from intestinal metaplasia to dysplasia. Here, we probe the molecular drivers of this
transition to dysplasia with unprecedented resolution using a combined approach of single-cell RNA sequencing,
mitochondrial mutational clone tracking and 3D epithelial culture systems. Results of this work will provide new
diagnostic and therapeutic targets for dysplastic BE to prevent development of esophageal adenocarcinoma.

title: Disentangling the HIV/opioid intertwined mechanisms on mitochondrial mediated inflammasome activation, neurotoxicity and targeting strategies: In vivo and in vitro analyses of fresh human brain
text:
Narrative.
Despite effective antiretrovirals, HIV spreads in the central nervous system and establishes persistent infection
precipitating HIV-associated cognitive impairment (CI). Using a unique collection of archived and fresh brain
specimens from Last Gift participants with thorough evaluation of opioid use and neurological conditions, this
study will determine the neurological consequences of HIV and opioids and how their interactions may amplify
or modify these effects on mitochondria-triggered inflammasome activation and neurotoxicity in resident brain
myeloid cells and neurons. Our overarching goal is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the intricate
relationship between these factors in the development of HIV-related CI and evaluate strategies to alleviate
opioids’ effects.

title: Unveiling the Atheroprone Role of Novel Mechanosensitive Histone Modification
text:
We recently identified a novel modification on histone H3 that increases in endothelial cells under disturbed blood
flow, causing abnormal cell function. We propose to study the effect of this modification on endothelial
dysfunction-caused atherosclerosis using both cell cultures and mouse models. This research will help us
understand how blood vessel cells malfunction and how atherosclerosis develops.

title: Strategies for Engineering Reliable Value Sets (SERVS)
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will develop tools to improve value sets:
lists of codes and corresponding terms from standard clinical vocabularies that define clinical concepts,
which form the basis of many clinical decision support (CDS) and clinical quality measurement (CQM)
systems. CDS and CQMs have the potential to support providers in delivering safe and effective care,
but value set issues can render them ineffective. Better value set tools, CDS, and CQMs together con-
tribute to NLM’s mission of enabling biomedical research and improving health care delivery for every-
one.

title: Machine learning-Based Neuromechanical Simulation for Rapid Personalized Exoskeleton Modeling to Enhance Walking Mobility in Community Environments
text:
This project aims to develop a physics-based, machine learning-driven simulation to automatically
generate 3D-printed, personalized exoskeleton prototypes, improving walking mobility for older
adults. By eliminating the need for extensive human-involved testing and large-scale datasets,
our innovative approach optimizes exoskeleton designs and assistance profiles for each individual,
making them more accessible and cost-effective. This work represents a shift from traditional lab-
based assistive devices to community-based approaches, addressing a key gap in rapidly
personalized exoskeleton modeling without the need for human testing.

title: HER2 PET imaging to assess HER2 heterogeneity and predict response to HER2-targeted ADC therapy in urothelial carcinoma
text:
This project will leverage our institutional experience in tumor profiling and molecular imaging to study the clinical
significance of molecular heterogeneity in urothelial cancer, with a focus on the HER2 receptor tyrosine kinase.
As a complement to tumor analyses, HER2 PET imaging will be used to study lesion-to-lesion differences in
HER2 expression and to determine if patients with heterogeneous HER2 expression are less likely to benefit
from treatment with HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Given the promising clinical activity of
HER2-targeted ADCs in patients with urothelial cancer, we predict that the studies proposed will accelerate the
clinical development of HER2-targeted ADCs and establish a clinical role for HER2 PET imaging as a guide to
patient selection.
.

title: SCH: New Advanced Machine Learning Framework for Mining Heterogeneous Ocular Data to Accelerate
text:
This project will focus on large-scale retinal imaging genetics data mining, develop and validate an automated
early ocular disease prediction and decision support system to identify risk factors and detect patients at risk
of ocular disease. The ultimate goal is to have the model monitor patients and identify those at high risk
during very early stage, thus the ophthalmologists can act on these patients before the irreversible outcome
occurs to provide the precision healthcare.

title: Culture-Independent Pathogen Identification Through Rapid Lipidomic Profiling
text:
New technologies are needed to improve the time to result for rapid diagnostic tests aimed at microbial
identification. We are developing a lipidomic surrogate for popular proteomic identification methods that allow
identification directly from clinical specimens, such as infected blood and urine samples. Our lipidomic assay
can be used as a stand-alone product relevant for general hospital settings, intensive care wards, and point-of-
care facilities on current FDA-approved MS instruments.

title: Dissecting the Synaptic and Cellular Actions of Dopamine in Vivo
text:
Dopamine is well-known for its importance in motivating, performing and reinforcing behavior, and its
dysfunction is implicated in many neuropsychiatric diseases including depression, addiction and Parkinson’s
Disease. How dopamine influences the activity of target neurons to modify behavior, however, remains
unclear. Developing an understanding of dopamine’s actions on synapses, cells and circuits will help to clarify
these actions and pave the way for novel targets for treatments that leverage these mechanisms.

title: Tau Mediates Microtubule and Mitochondrial Dynamics to Control Cellular Organization and Alveolar Epithelial Repair
text:
Degenerative lung diseases are adding significant burden to the health care in the United States. Currently there
are no effective treatments and lung transplantation remains the best resource to improve lung function and
survival. Understanding the genetic and cell biological mechanisms that initiate and promote disease
pathogenesis in the aged lungs will aid in discovery of novel treatments to block or reverse these diseases.
